## Welcome to PPADEM

[About the Project]{.ppadem-pill}

Political Parties and Democracy in Africa (PPADEM) is an ambitious, collaborative multi-year research project investigating the role of political parties in shaping democracy across Africa, covering 80 political parties across 25 nations.

- **Primary Brand Red**: `#990000` (headings, accents)
- **Secondary Teal**: `#298c8c` (subtitles, secondary metrics)

## Code & Data Analysis

```r
# Visualising party competition indicators
library(ggplot2)

ggplot(party_data, aes(x = year, y = competitiveness, color = region)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1.2) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("#990000", "#298c8c", "#f1a226")) +
  theme_minimal()
```

## Results so far {.ppadem-section .teal}

## Key Findings

::: {.ppadem-key-findings}
[Key findings]{.ppadem-label}

1. Party finance rules vary more within regions than between them.
2. Youth membership is growing fastest where parties run local branches.
3. Trust in parties tracks perceived electoral integrity.
:::

::: {.ppadem-quote}
Parties are where democracy is organised, or where it fails.

[— PPADEM research team]{.attribution}
:::

## Summary & Next Steps

- Finalise field assessments across pilot regions
- Publish comparative report on party funding regulations
- Convene annual regional stakeholder policy dialogue
